## Fix duplicate rows in the nightly billing export

The nightly billing export wrote duplicate rows when the job retried after a timeout. The retry appended a second batch, and nothing keyed the write, so nothing stopped the repeat.

## Changes

- The export now upserts, keyed on `(account_id, period)`.
- A new unique index covers those two columns.
- A backfill script removes the 1,412 duplicate rows written between 3 and 19 March.
- The export file format is unchanged.

## Testing

I added an integration test that kills the job mid-batch and reruns it.

## Rollout

The index build locks the table for about 40 seconds at production size. Please run the migration in Thursday's maintenance window rather than in a normal deploy.

## Replace payment status polling with the provider webhook

The payment status page polled the provider every 5 seconds for each open tab. This PR replaces that polling with the provider's webhook, so status now lands in about 1 second instead of taking up to 5.

## What changed

- New endpoint `POST /hooks/payment` verifies the signature header and drops events older than 10 minutes.
- Polling stays behind the flag `payments.poll_fallback`, which defaults to off.

## Impact

Provider API calls from this page fell from about 90k a day to about 2k in staging.

## Testing

I tested with the provider's sandbox replay tool.

## Not done

Retries for webhook deliveries we fail to process are not part of this PR. They are tracked in a follow-up ticket. Until that ticket is done, a delivery we fail to process is not retried, which is the main thing to weigh when reviewing.

## Move HTTP retry logic into the shared client package

Three services each carried their own copy of the HTTP retry logic. This PR moves it into the shared client package and deletes 340 lines across the three services.

## Behavior change

This is a pure refactor with one exception: the default timeout goes from 30s to 10s.

The reports service overrides the timeout back to 30s, because its largest query takes about 22s and would otherwise time out under the new default.

## Unchanged

The retry policy is the same as before:

- 3 attempts
- exponential backoff starting at 200ms
- retries only on 502, 503, 504 and connection resets

## Testing

Existing tests pass. I added one test for the reports override.

## Review focus

Please check the timeout default first, since it is the only change that can alter behavior. The other two services now get the 10s default.

Subject: Log storage renewal: where we landed after the vendor call

Hi all,

Here is a summary of today's call with the log storage vendor about the renewal.

They offered 18% off for a two-year term and 7% off for one year. We did not accept either. Our usage grew 31% over the last year, so the per-GB overage price matters more to us than the base discount. We told them we need that price in writing before deciding, and they will send it by Wednesday.

Next steps:

- Priya owns the cost comparison against self-hosting, due the 14th.
- We will make the decision at the meeting on the 16th.
- The contract lapses on the 30th.

Please do not agree to anything with the vendor before the 16th, including informal commitments.

Thanks,

Subject: Review needed by Friday: new nullable column on orders

Hi analytics team,

We want to add a nullable column, cancelled_at, to the orders table. Your nightly job selects * from orders and writes to a fixed-width file, so we are worried a new column could break it.

Could you confirm by Friday whether the job tolerates an extra column?

If it does not, we can ship a view without the column for you to read from. That costs us about a day. Our release is the following Tuesday, and without an answer by Friday we will build the view to be safe, so a quick reply saves us the work.

The schema diff and a sample row are attached.

Thanks,

Search incident follow-up

Search was down for 47 minutes on Tuesday, from 14:12 to 14:59. About 3,100 searches failed. No data was lost.

Cause: a config push set the shard count to 6 for an index that was built with 8, so the nodes refused to start. The change was reviewed, but the review tool showed only the changed line, not the index it applied to. We rolled the config back to recover.

Detection was slow. Alerting fired after 9 minutes because the health check only tested the load balancer, not a query.

Actions, both owned by the search team:

- The health check now runs a real query. Done.
- Config validation compares the shard count to the live index. In review.

Two gaps led to this: the review could not show what the change applied to, and the health check could not tell that search had stopped working. Each action closes one of them.

Accounts database migration: weekly update

Status: slipped by one week.

Done this week:

- Dual writes are enabled for all 14 tables.
- Row counts match on 12 of the 14.

The two that differ are sessions and invoices. Sessions is expected, since rows expire during the copy. Invoices is off by 23 rows and we cannot yet explain it.

Slipped: the read cutover moves from the 9th to the 16th because of the invoices mismatch.

Risk: if the mismatch is a dual-write bug, other tables may be affected in ways the row counts do not show. We are running a checksum comparison this week to find out.

Needed from others: the billing team to freeze invoice schema changes until the 16th, so the investigation is not chasing a moving table.

Hey, I found why CI got slow. Builds went from about 6 minutes to about 19 since last Monday.

The cause is that the cache key for the dependency layer now includes the build timestamp, so the cache never hits. It came in with the change that added build metadata to the image labels.

The fix is up for review. It moves the labels to the final stage, so the dependency layer key is stable again.

Until it merges, rebasing on main will not help, and there is nothing to do locally. Your builds are slow because of the cache key, not anything on your branch.

Once it merges, expect about 6 minutes again. A look at the PR would speed that up.
